 Microsoft Outlook down as thousands of users report issues
 Microsoft 
 Technology 
 Scotland 
 By Gregor Young 
 Share
 0 Comments 
 Microsoft users have experienced issues with the service today (October 29) (Image: Getty Images) 
 This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today,
 and has been written by our American colleagues.
 It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.
 THOUSANDS of people have reported major issues with the Microsoft Outlook email service amid what appears to be a significant outage.
 At the time of writing nearly 150,000 people have made reports to the Down Detector web service about the email platform.
 Across social media users reported experiencing problems such as error codes and frozen screens when trying to send an email.
 CoPilot also seems to be affected by the outage, with Down Detector also showing a spike in reports from users.
 Teams is not currently affected by the issue, though The National is monitoring the situation closely.
 The last major Outlook outage was in August , affecting worldwide users of the service.
 Microsoft issues statement on Outlook outage
 Microsoft has now issued a statement, explaining that the issue began in the US but can now affect users in any region.
 "We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543," the company wrote on social media.
 "While we're working to mitigate impact, we've confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region, more information will be provided in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543."
 However, the admin centre also seems to be affected by the outage.
 Many users were frustrated with the communication, with one responding: "The same admin center we cannot log into currently, good tip."
 "Maybe update your status portal to not say 'resolved'," added another.
